## Playwright-browser-use 1.0.11 Changelog

- Added `package-lock.json` to the repository.
- Removed `skill-card.md` file.
- SKILL.md: Documented new `capabilities` section outlining supported features.
- No core logic or runtime changes; updates are for documentation and repository metadata only.

llm.summary: This is a powerful local browser-automation skill that clearly discloses its code-execution, browser-session, and local-daemon risks for trusted local use.

dimensions.detail: A localhost daemon controlling a visible Chrome/Edge browser is proportionate for this skill, but it should be used only in a trusted local session because it can act with the current page's credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package uses a normal Node/Playwright dependency setup, has no package scripts in package.json, and the shell shim only resolves the skill directory, sets NODE_PATH, and executes pw-browser.js.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions repeatedly require observing pages before acting, user handoff for login or verification, confirmation before destructive edits, and trusted-page use for eval/run-code; Bash(curl:*) is broader than the examples need, but it does not materially exceed the already disclosed browser/network authority.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The daemon persists across commands and writes a token file under ~/.pw-browser/daemon.json; this is disclosed and has close/safe-mode controls, though users should close the daemon when finished and prefer safe mode when code execution is unnecessary.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's purpose is browser automation, and its high-impact capabilities are purpose-aligned: page JavaScript eval, Playwright run-code, credentialed browser actions, screenshots/downloads, and form/content mutation are all disclosed as part of that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you are comfortable letting the assistant control a visible local browser, interact with logged-in websites, read page cookies/storage through eval, submit forms, and write files through screenshots or downloads. Use PW_BROWSER_SAFE_MODE=1 when custom code execution is not needed, avoid untrusted code snippets or high-privilege pages, and close the daemon after use.
llm.findings: [SDI-4] expected: The reported concern is partly valid as an implementation-comment limitation: run-code receives a live Playwright page object, which can still cause local file writes through browser features. The user-facing SKILL.md, README, and running-code reference do disclose file writes, credentialed page access, arbitrary browser/network actions, safe mode, and trusted-local-use limits, so this does not justify escalation by itself.
